description:
`storage` gives an app you enroll in its own folder of files for that enrollment, where it keeps its working files and results, and you can read them back.

The gateway answers `storage` itself (`storage://enrollment`): there is no upstream, and file bytes never pass through it. Each enrollment's files are `enrollments/{enrollment_id}/` in private UnitySVC storage. A call is a control request (`list`, `get`, `put`, `post`, `delete`) that the backend authorizes against the calling key's `service:storage` grant: it computes the object key itself and answers either a listing or a short-lived presigned URL that the client uses to move the bytes directly to or from storage. Its exports declare two permissions and nothing else: `read` (list, get) and `write` (put, post, delete); `invoke`, and the `service:*` and `*` wildcards that stand for it, never reach `storage`. It has no options: the folder is never chosen by a policy. A key bound to an enrollment reaches only that enrollment's folder, and naming another enrollment is refused. Your own unbound key names the enrollment with the `X-UnitySVC-Enrollment` header and reaches only enrollments it may see. `storage` is not billed while it is experimental.

`POST /storage/list` with `{"path": "results/"}` and a key whose policy grants `service:storage`, e.g. `{"object": "service:storage", "permissions": ["read", "write"]}`, lists that folder of the enrollment; an unbound key adds `X-UnitySVC-Enrollment: <code>`. `POST /storage/get` answers a download URL; `POST /storage/put` with `{"path", "content_type", "size"}` (or `POST /storage/post` for a browser form upload) answers an upload ticket, and `POST /storage/delete` removes a file; the last three need `write`. See How to use this service for the request and answer shapes.
name: storage

payout_price.description: Not billed (yet): reaching an enrollment's files is free while the service is experimental

summary: Give an app you enroll its own folder of files for the enrollment through `/storage`, which you can read back.
